title: Section-component loci in a cartesian square
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] with a section $\sigma:Y\to X$. Let $a:X\prime\to X$, $f\prime:X\prime\to Y\prime$, $b:Y\prime\to Y$ form a cartesian square [def-pc-fibre-product], and let $\sigma\prime:Y\prime\to X\prime$ be a section of $f\prime$ with $a\circ\sigma\prime=\sigma\circ b$. Define $C(f,\sigma)=\{x\in X\mid x\text{ lies in the connected component of }\sigma(f(x))\text{ in }f^{-1}(f(x))\}$. Then $a^{-1}C(f,\sigma)=C(f\prime,\sigma\prime)$.

proof.text: Work directly in the given cartesian square. Fix x′ and put y′=f′(x′), p=σ′(y′). Commutativity and section compatibility give f(a(x′))=b(y′), a(p)=σ(b(y′)), and f′(p)=y′. In the locally noetherian old fibre, its section component is open; choose an ambient open U representing it. Its section point gives a residue-field section of U→Y. Restrict the given cartesian square to W=a⁻¹(U). The fibre of U→Y is connected and has that rational point. Apply [lem-sbc-connected-rational-point-geometrically-connected] and isPullback_fiberToSpecResidueField_of_isPullback to obtain connectedness of the fibre of W→Y′. Its image in X′ is preconnected, contains p, and lies in the new fibre. Maximality of connectedComponentIn gives the forward inclusion.

For the reverse inclusion, the continuous image under a of the new component is preconnected. It contains σ(b(y′)) by the compatible section and is contained in the old fibre by square commutativity. IsPreconnected.subset_connectedComponentIn gives membership of a(x′) in the old component. Set extensionality combines the inclusions. No canonical pullback reduction or transport homeomorphism is needed.
